**36. Which tool bakes the text atlas for in-world panels?** *(§6, decision 6-3.)*
*Options.* Adopt the pure-Rust generator as a build-time-only dependency; vendor roughly six hundred lines
and own it; use the bindings to the unmaintained C++ original; or depend on an existing world-space
interface crate.
*Recommendation.* **Adopt the pure-Rust generator as a build dependency only.** It never links into the
shipped client because the atlas is a baked artefact, so the runtime dependency surface stays at zero and
any drift becomes a build-reproducibility question rather than a runtime one. Reject the C++ bindings — a
C++ dependency undermines cross-binary reproducibility.
*Blocks.* The panel slice only.
*Cost of deferring.* Low; not a one-way door.

---

**The five decisions the detail-level ladder creates.**

**37. What does one edit-pyramid entry hold, how is it keyed and stored, and what happens when it
disagrees with the deltas it was derived from?**
**[USER DECISION 8-A]** *(New — Addendum 2 §C.4 and §E. Ranked third: it is permanent delta data and it
freezes with the chunk format. **Collapsed 2026-08-03: this row absorbs §2's 2-H and 2-I, §3's 3-J and
§4's 4-E**, which asked the same question four incompatible ways; those four markers are deleted in their
own sections and point here.)*
The generated world coarsens itself for free; **player edits do not.** Without a pyramid, a tunnel a
player dug vanishes at 200 m and reappears at 100 m and a base pops in and out as they fly — an artefact
the seamless law forbids outright. The fix is a sparse summary per coarse cell, maintained by the realm
owner: on commit of an edit batch, walk up the ladder recomputing each touched coarse cell **from its
eight children's summaries**, stopping at the first rung whose summary is unchanged. A child that has no
entry resolves through the **generator** — one octave-dropped evaluation — never through the delta log and
never to a default. Rendering a coarse tier is then "generate by dropping octaves, then overwrite only
where the pyramid has an entry", and an entry that comes to equal what the generator would produce is
*deleted*, so digging a hole and filling it back in leaves nothing behind at any rung. *(§3 owns the
record and the persistence, §4 owns the coarsening kernel and the shape a coarse cell is drawn through.
This row is the decision, not the code.)*
*Struck, because it was wrong in the direction that matters.* The earlier text said the maintainer
"regenerates the affected fine cells from the seed, applies the deltas and recomputes one entry per tier —
at most eight small writes, **no disk read**". **The no-disk-read claim cannot produce the record**: a
parent is a function of its eight children, so the walk-up reads eight sibling summaries per rung. The
honest cost, which is also the §8.4 gate: **≤ 1 entry write and ≤ 1 pyramid storage-block read per rung
per touched coarse cell** — the eight siblings always lie in *one* storage block, because a chunk edge of
62 cells is even — **zero reads of the edit log and zero reads of any tier-0 delta**, all of it inside the
log's own write transaction. Worst case with every sibling missing is (rungs − 1) × 8 × 5 noise
evaluations at S0.0's measured 12.19 ns: **5.85 µs on a thirteen-rung starter body, 9.75 µs at
twenty-one rungs**, under one percent of a one-millisecond edit budget. With the early exit, the common
single edit inside solid rock terminates at the first or second rung, about half a microsecond.
*Storage is proportional to edits, not to world size* — and how proportional depends on the **shape** of
the edit set, which spans a factor of fifty, so one number would mislead a capacity plan. The four cases:
a compact three-dimensional cluster costs **0.143** entries per edit, a surface or wall **0.333**, a
one-cell-thick line about **1.000**, and edits sharing no coarse cell at all are hard-bounded at one entry
per rung. At eight bytes an entry and thirteen rungs: **a 1,000-block one-wide tunnel is 504 entries ≈
3.9 KiB; an 8,000-block 20×20×20 tower is 1,168 entries ≈ 9.1 KiB; a hundred million mixed edits are
about 880 MB.** Deeper ladders do not move the clustered rows — the series converge — and only the
adversarial isolated row grows, bounded by the rung count by construction.
*What is actually open — five sub-questions, and only the first is expensive.*
- **(a) The entry's contents.** *Options.* **(A1) — recommended — 8 bytes, one machine word: an 18-bit
  cell index, a 16-bit dominant substance, an 8-bit octant mask, an 8-bit mean fill and 14 reserved bits
  rejected on decode if non-zero.** The octant mask is what keeps an eight-metre ramp reading as a ramp
  and a wall of thin panels from vanishing; the storage is the arithmetic above. **(A2) drop the octant
  mask, keep count plus substance (7 B/entry).** Saves about 12 % of the pyramid — roughly 105 MB over a
  hundred million edits — and every distant player build becomes solid-or-empty: this is the documented
  "castles read as voxel-based blobs" failure, and it is what a count thresholded to a boolean always
  produces. **(A3) also store a min/max solid-height pair (A2 + 2 B).** *Rejected here on structure rather
  than cost* — min/max solid height is a per-**column** quantity and this is a per-**cell** record, so it
  replicates up to 62× per column, and it is exactly reconstructible from A1 plus the generator. **(A4)
  a tag-length-value entry.** Costs the fixed-width property that makes the sorted drain cheap and
  deterministic.
  *Struck:* this row previously recommended A2's ancestor — solid count, dominant material **and a
  persisted min/max pair** — and called the pair "the conservative envelope that makes skirts provably
  sufficient". **The envelope survives in full and only its home changes:** it is §3.5.2's per-(tier,
  chunk column) min/max structure, **derived and never persisted**, a pure function of the seed and the
  pyramid, recomputable at any time and therefore outside the format-freeze problem entirely. That also
  kills the separate `column_relief` table §2.7.1 was reserving for the same data, and restores §2's
  "exactly one new persisted structure" claim.
- **(b) How the fill is spent when the coarse cell is drawn.** *Options.* **(B1) — recommended — map the
  (octant mask, fill bucket) pair onto §4's existing shape catalogue through a baked 4,608-byte table
  folded into the block-registry hash.** Zero extra stored bytes, because it reinterprets fields the entry
  already holds; a tower keeps reading as a tower. **(B2) threshold to solid-or-empty.** Zero bytes saved,
  and it is A2's failure mode arriving through the read side instead of the write side. **There is
  deliberately NO tunable threshold anywhere on this path** — an octant mask of zero means empty and every
  other mask selects a shape through the table, so there is no solid-or-empty decision left to diverge on.
  *(An earlier draft put a client-side `solid_threshold` render-tuning field on this decision. It is
  struck: it is the one place a **detail** knob could produce a visible **fact** difference between two
  clients, which is exactly what folding the table into the registry hash — a refused connection on
  mismatch — exists to prevent.)* The table is therefore core-crate Tier-A code at 100 % coverage,
  identical on server and client, exercised at every tier.
- **(c) The storage granularity.** *Options.* **(C1) — recommended — the storage block is one (tier,
  chunk) pair holding that chunk's sparse entry list, in the same database file as the deltas**, reusing
  the same sparse and masked-dense encodings and the same crossover the chunk record already uses. A
  1,000-block tunnel becomes about 40 records rather than about 500 keys, it moves with the realm on a
  re-shard, it flushes under the same fence, and one whole rung is one contiguous range scan. **(C2) one
  key per entry.** Simpler, and it puts hundreds of millions of keys in the store on a heavily built
  planet.
- **(d) The write invariant.** *Options.* **(D1) — recommended — only tier 0 is writable, expressed in the
  store's type signature:** the write takes a tier-0-proven key, so writing to a coarse rung does not
  compile. One newtype today. **(D2) a convention plus a review checklist**, which is what every project
  that later found a coarse-tier write in production had. D1 converts §E's "derived data can silently
  disagree with its source" risk into something the compiler enforces on the write path, leaving only the
  read-path audit — a recompute-from-deltas command plus the equality assertion in the test suite (§8.4).
- **(e) The divergence policy.** *(Absorbed from §2's 2-I.)* *Options.* **(E1) — recommended — recompute
  the entry and increment a divergence counter the harness asserts is zero**: a failing build in
  development, an invisible self-heal in production. **(E2) refuse to open the store**, as an
  identity-digest mismatch does. The digest guards data that reinterprets a player's wall; the pyramid
  only summarises data the store still holds, so E2 destroys access to a world over reconstructible
  cosmetic data.
*Recommendation.* **A1 + B1 + C1 + D1 + E1.** The 12 % storage difference between A1 and A2 buys the
entire silhouette on a record that can never be changed afterwards, using a mask the shape bake already
computes. The one genuine judgement inside it is taste: **A1 means a distant player build reads as
FACETED** — its slopes and corners survive — **while A2 means it reads as BLOCKY.** On a world whose art
direction is deliberately blocky someone could reasonably prefer A2's harder distant read; this design
does not, because it contradicts what the player built, but it is a real position and it is the reason
this is a decision rather than a ruling.
*Blocks.* Whether player edits survive coarsening at all; the delta store's layout; the chunk key.
*Cost of deferring.* **A one-way door of the same class as decision 2.** It is permanent delta data:
deciding after the first world is saved is a migration over every planet, ship, station and blueprint
that has ever been edited. It must freeze with the chunk format, not with the phase that first writes an
entry.

**38. Is sharpness constant, or is memory constant — and what are the tier-selection defaults?**
**[USER DECISION 8-B]** *(New — Addendum 2 §C.2 and §C.6. Low cost of lateness; listed because they are
fields, and the no-magic-numbers rule means they must exist as fields before the first literal is typed.
**Collapsed 2026-08-03: absorbs §1's 1-A and §5's 5-H**, which asked the same question from the overview
and from the render pipeline; both markers are deleted there and point here.)*
The ladder picks a rung from how big a cell would look on screen. **Do we hold that target fixed and let
memory vary, or hold memory fixed and let the target vary?** And what are the shipped defaults for the
fields the ladder introduces?
*Options.* **(H1) fixed target, no governor.** One on-screen target always; the world looks equally sharp
everywhere. In a dense, heavily built region it blows the resident-byte cap and the client either hitches
or evicts something visible; on an empty plain it leaves quality on the table. **This is the failure the
title the owner cited actually shipped** — a fixed memory target enforced by a uniformly aggressive
ladder, so everything looks cut instead of the cheapest thing looking cut, and raising quality settings
paradoxically *worsens* pop-in. **(H2) — recommended — fixed target plus a smoothed, hysteretic
governor** that raises pixels-per-cell toward a ceiling when resident bytes exceed the cap and lowers it
back with hysteresis. Detail is shed where it is cheapest — the outer rungs step down first — and the
crossfade hides the step. Tens of lines. **It must be smoothed or it becomes a pop source.** **(H3) H2
plus a user-facing "terrain detail" slider** bounding both ends: H2 plus a settings entry, at the first
settings pass.
*Fields and defaults*, all on the **render tuning struct** — no fifth tuning struct, and never inline
literals: **`px_per_cell_target` 2.0** (lower is sharper and *quadratically* more expensive; it is the one
knob that trades sharpness against everything else, and it gives tier L out to 786·2^L metres),
**`px_per_cell_ceiling` 4.0**, **`resident_chunk_byte_cap`** sized from the terrain row of the video-memory
table, **`governor_hysteresis` 0.15**, **`crossfade_band_fraction` 0.15**. *(Five fields, not four, and one
rename: this row used to call the governor's bound `px_per_cell_floor`. The governor **raises**
pixels-per-cell to shed detail, so the bound it runs into is a **ceiling**; and the hysteresis it must have
is now a named field rather than an adjective.)*
*The fade-direction rule, which is not a tuning value and must be written into the slice.* With a band
covering the last fraction f of a tier's range, the doubly-resident area is R²(1−(1−f)²) against an
annulus of 0.75R². **The direction of the fade changes the cost fourfold: the COARSE rung fades in early
over the fine rung's outer band; the fine rung dies at its own range — never the reverse.** Faded-in
coarse columns have a 4× larger footprint, so at f = 0.2 they cost about 45 extra columns per boundary —
roughly **+10 %** on the 3,158-column figure across seven boundaries. Keeping the *fine* rung alive into
the coarse annulus instead costs about 182 per boundary, roughly **+40 %**. At f = 0.15 the cost is about
+7 %.
*And `crossfade_band_fraction` is not free to choose, which is a correction to how this row used to read
it.* The residency gate of §8.4 is what **bounds** it, not the reverse: measured while moving, f = 0.15
gives **7,353** resident chunks and passes the ≤ 7,500 gate, and f = 0.20 gives **7,510** and fails it.
**The shipped default is 0.15 because 0.2 does not pass.**
*Recommendation.* **H2 now, H3 at the first settings pass.** Three constraints ride with it and all three
are non-obvious enough to be written down beside it rather than discovered.
- **The governor clamps the shadow distance.** Raising the pixel target shrinks tier 0's range, and a
  fixed shadow distance would silently walk a crossfade band into the shadow-casting set, where the
  engine's shadow pass does not honour the dither and the result is a permanent band of double-darkening
  and acne at exactly the distance the player is flying toward (decision 41).
- **The governor may never shrink tier 0 below `tier0_min_radius` = maximum tool reach + one chunk edge**,
  or building stops working at range; an ungoverned governor eventually decides the cheapest thing to drop
  is the disc around the player.
- **The governor may never change collision, physics or any gameplay-visible fact.** It is cosmetic,
  client-local policy, and its scope is asserted rather than assumed. Its output reaches the server only
  as the clamped, non-authoritative `tier_floor` hint of S0.4, which may select **what is sent** and never
  **what is true**.
**On a decision-21 B1 build this governor is not optional**, because the 100 km view is 1.3–3.0 GB at that
vertex format (see row 21).
*Blocks.* Nothing structural. It is listed so the fields exist before someone types a constant.
*Cost of deferring.* Low — but the *fade-direction rule* is not a tuning value and should be written into
the slice, not left to whoever implements the margins.

**39. Do distant props get baked impostors?** **[USER DECISION 8-C]** *(New — Addendum 2 §C.7's boundary,
made concrete. Coupled to decision 25.)*
*The question.* Beyond the prop radius, a twelve-metre tree currently vanishes — ledger entry D-DEC-7
calls it "the most jarring pop available", and it is the one hole the density-falloff answer does not
close, because a tree is not a density, it is an object.
*Options.* **(A)** Nothing — props stop at their radius, and the far field is terrain only. **(B)** Baked
**hemi-octahedral impostors** for a curated archetype set: albedo, normal, depth and ORM baked over a
lattice of view directions, sampled by projecting the camera direction onto a half-octahedron and
blending the three lattice points of the containing triangle, with one parallax offset from the depth map
so silhouettes hold. **(C)** Cluster impostors / billboard clouds for whole distant forests.
*Recommendation.* **(B), at 1024² atlases, ≤ 32 archetypes, vegetation and props only — and it is a
decision, not an engineering call, because it costs an offline bake tool and video memory.**
*Why it is legal under decision 7's exclusion list.* §6's decoration is deterministically **derived** from
the block field and is non-interactive, so an impostor of a derived tuft is *a coarser rung of the real
thing* — derived-from, not substituted-for. **The same technique applied to terrain, structures, ships or
anything player-built is forbidden and stays forbidden**: you cannot bake an atlas of a base a player
finished thirty seconds ago, doing it at runtime is a render-to-texture stall in exactly the moment the
seamless law forbids one, and a distant player base is something a player could act on, so it must be the
pyramid rung of the real thing.
*The quality bar, from the one shipped title with a well-reviewed far field:* its distant trees are
**lit and shadowed** under the same lighting model rather than flat sprites, which is why they read as
volumetric. That means baking normal and depth and lighting the impostor with the same code as the mesh
— which also makes the transition hideable by the same dither band the tier crossfade already uses.
*The numbers that decide the resolution.* With mips, a **2048²** set (BC7 albedo, BC5 normal, BC7 ORM,
BC4 depth) is 18.67 MiB per archetype; 32 archetypes is **597 MiB** — more than §5.3.6's entire 512 MiB
material set and enough on its own to breach the 3.0 GiB cap on top of the **1.41 GiB on-foot** baseline
*(corrected from 1.20 GiB, which predates §5.3.6's re-sum for the ladder)*. At
**1024²** the same four maps are 4.67 MiB per archetype and 32 archetypes cost **149 MiB**, which fits.
Frame resolution sets the rung: a 128²-texel frame stays convincing to about 128 screen pixels, and a
20 m tree subtending 128 px on a 1920 px / 70° screen is at about **250 m** — so impostors extend props
roughly 3× past §6.10's current 80 m prop radius rather than replacing them.
*Costs and caveats, stated.* An offline bake tool; the atlases are a derived work of whatever archetype
set decision 25 lands on and inherit its licence clauses; impostor atlases do not carry mipmaps in the
standard implementations, so they alias at exactly the distances they are used and need an explicit
mitigation. Zero server cost, zero wire cost, zero determinism exposure — the mapping uses only absolute
value, add, multiply and sign, no transcendentals. **(C) is rejected**: billboard clouds need an offline
clustering pass per archetype and produce layered semi-transparent quads whose overdraw is worst exactly
where they are meant to save, and at our rung distance a hemi-octahedral impostor is strictly better per
byte and per pixel. **(A) is defensible** if the archetype set stays small and the prop radius is pushed
instead — say so if that is the preference, because it deletes a tool.
*Blocks.* The prop catalogue's size; an offline bake tool; ~149 MiB of video memory.
*Cost of deferring.* Moderate and one-directional: the bake consumes the archetype set, so deciding after
the set is authored means re-authoring for bake-friendliness (clean silhouettes, no interpenetrating
geometry).

**40. Virtual texturing, a cached material bake, or neither?** **[USER DECISION 8-D]** *(New. Ranked
last, and it is listed **because it is a do-not-build ruling** — the ladder makes "we should virtualise
the textures too" an obvious next thought, and it is wrong here for reasons worth recording once.)*
*Options.* **(A)** Hardware sparse / partially-resident textures. **(B)** A software virtual-texture
system — indirection texture, physical page atlas, feedback render target, readback, manual mip
selection, page borders, eviction. **(C)** A runtime-virtual-texture-style **cached material bake** per
terrain tile: composite the material once into a tile cache and re-read it. **(D)** Neither.
*Recommendation.* **(D) neither, now — with (C) named as a later option behind a measured trigger.**
*And the positive half of the same finding, which this row otherwise carries only in the negative.* The
reference title's texture quality comes from **texel density plus screen-space displacement, not from a
residency system**, which is why (D) costs us nothing in look: §5.3.6's 256 texels per cell and §5.4's
parallax relief are the same two mechanisms. The one action it generates is a settings entry — **the
displacement scale ships as a user-facing slider from day one** (§5.3.9), because they had to retrofit
exactly that in a patch.
- **(A) is not available, and this is a hardware-level fact rather than a judgement.** The vendored
  wgpu 27.0.1 exposes no sparse, tiled or partially-resident texture feature at all; the WebGPU
  investigation into it is parked with no assignee because the three backends disagree irreconcilably.
  The impressive published results in this family (a 70–80 % texture-memory reduction) rest on reserved
  resources plus sampler feedback, neither of which exists on our stack.
- **(B) solves a problem we do not have.** Virtual texturing buys *unique* texels; we have none. §5.3.1
  derives UV by exact integer modulo of a four-cell world period and variation comes from the macro layer
  and per-block hash, so the 512 MiB material array is **already the complete resident set for an
  entire Earth-sized planet at any view distance, and the ladder adds not one byte to it.** A 4096² BC7
  physical cache would be 16 MiB per map, 48 MiB for the trio — a smaller constant, bought with a
  multi-thousand-line Tier-B subsystem, a GPU→CPU readback loop with 2–3 frames of latency, and the loss
  of hardware `AddressMode::Repeat` (page borders break wrapping — the exact atlas failure §5.3.2 already
  rejected) and of clean anisotropic filtering across page seams.
- **(C) is the cheaper 80 % idea and the arithmetic says not yet.** Our per-pixel composite is already
  cheap: three taps per material, six at a §5.5 seam, plus two macro taps — about **8 taps on the worst
  pixel**. A tile cache collapses that to 3 + 1 indirection = 4. Saving ~4 taps over ~1.45 M terrain
  pixels is 5.8 M fetches per frame, roughly **0.03–0.06 ms** — below noise. And a cache only pays when
  re-reads greatly exceed re-bakes, while every block edit invalidates the tiles it touches: §5.10.5's
  sustained-edit budget (mining beams, explosions) is precisely the regime where it thrashes. **Trigger to
  revisit, written down so it is a measurement and not a mood: terrain fragment tap count above ~16, or a
  profile showing the composite above ~1 ms.** Note that decision 22's material feature ladder pushes in
  the opposite direction — it takes coarse tiers *down* to about 2 taps.
*One calibration finding that belongs here, because it reorders effort.* On the shipped title studied,
per-pixel ray-traced diffuse global illumination across a 200 km² world costs 3–4 fps and the CPU is
barely stressed; the frame goes to crowds, battles and **streaming-heavy transitions**. Lighting ambition
is not what sinks the frame — **residency and upload under motion is** — which is exactly what §5.3.6
already says ("the budget is not tight; the UPLOAD budget is") and is where the next benchmark slot
should go (§8.4).
*Blocks.* Nothing today.
*Cost of deferring.* None. The cost of *not recording it* is someone spending a month on (B).

**41. How far do player-built structures cast real shadows?** **[USER DECISION 8-E]** *(New — forced by a
hard engine constraint the ladder walks straight into. **Collapsed 2026-08-03: absorbs §5's 5-I**, which
asked the same question from the render pipeline; that marker is deleted there and points here.)*
*The constraint, verified in the vendored crate.* `bevy_pbr` 0.18.1 declares
`MAX_CASCADES_PER_LIGHT = 4` as a compile-time constant backing a fixed four-element array in both the
Rust light uniform and the WGSL view struct — raising it is an engine fork carried across every release,
not a config change. The shipped defaults are four cascades over **0.1 m to 150 m**, split at 10.0, 24.7,
60.8 and 150.0 m. **The ladder draws to 100 km. Ninety-nine point five percent of the view has no
shadow-map coverage**, and pushing the maximum to 1 km with only four cascades makes the first cascade
cover 0.1–5.6 m and quadruples texel footprint everywhere else.
*Options.* **(I1)** Accept the engine default: four cascades to 150 m. Zero cost, visibly short in an open
landscape. **(I2) — recommended — four cascades out to a DERIVED horizon, plus long-range terrain
self-shadowing computed from the coarse height function** rather than rasterised. **(I3)** Fork the engine
for more cascades: a fork carried across every release, for kilometres of a 100 km view. Rejected on
maintenance.
*Recommendation.* **(I2), with the horizon DERIVED and GOVERNOR-CLAMPED rather than authored.**
*Struck: the earlier "**300–500 m**" figure.* It was an authored literal in a design whose standing rule
forbids exactly that, and §5.9.6(b) derives the same number from quantities that already exist. **The
relation, asserted at start-up and re-asserted whenever the residency governor changes the pixel target:**

    R₀                  = 1 / (px_per_cell_target × θ_px)          — tier 0's outer range; MOVES WITH THE GOVERNOR
    shadow_max_distance = min(shadow_max_distance_authored,
                              (1 − crossfade_band_fraction) × R₀)

At the defaults (`px_per_cell_target` 2.0, `θ_px` 6.363e-4 rad, `crossfade_band_fraction` 0.15) that is
**R₀ = 786 m, so `shadow_max_distance` ≤ 668 m** — and the authored value is free to be lower. No tier
crossing is then inside the shadow-casting set, so the engine's missing dither in the shadow pass cannot
bite. **It is a derived relation clamped by the governor, never two numbers configured side by side** —
which is the whole point: with a fixed distance, raising the pixel target shrinks R₀ and silently walks a
crossfade band into the shadow-casting set, six months later, as a mystifying bug.
*Why the second half is nearly free and unique to a generated world:* tier L's height is the same
closed-form octave sum with the top L octaves dropped, so the client can march that coarse field along
the sun direction and get a horizon angle per point — no shadow map, no cascade, no memory, and **by
construction it can never disagree with the drawn mesh, because it is the same function that produced
it.** Cost is a few dozen ALU per pixel, or a per-chunk-column horizon-angle texture updated with the
chunk. It gives correct mountain-shadow-across-a-valley at 20 km, which no four-cascade system can. What
it cannot capture is player-built geometry — hence the residual decision: **builds cast real shadows only
inside the cascade horizon.** Every open-world game already works this way; saying so is honest rather
than a hack. (I3) is rejected: an engine fork maintained forever, for a technique that would still cover
kilometres of a 100 km view.
*Two invariants that ship with it, both cheap and both bugs if omitted.*
- **A chunk's shadow-caster mesh IS its visual mesh — one mesh object, both passes — asserted, not
  assumed.** Bevy gives this by default; the assertion exists so nobody later "optimises" the shadow pass
  by selecting a coarser tier, which is the classic version of this bug. If a separate shadow tier is
  ever introduced it must be selected by the **light's** screen-space error, never the camera's.
- **The shadow pass does not dither.** `VISIBILITY_RANGE_DITHER` is set into the pipeline key in exactly
  three places in `bevy_pbr` 0.18.1 — the main pass, the prepass and the wireframe — and `render/light.rs`,
  which queues the shadow phase, never sets it. So during a tier crossfade **both rungs are fully opaque
  shadow casters**, two surfaces up to a coarse cell apart, and the shadow map gets the union: double
  darkening plus self-shadow acne along every tier boundary, permanently, at exactly the distance the
  player is flying toward. **The fix is the derived horizon above, which closes it BY CONSTRUCTION**: with
  `shadow_max_distance ≤ (1 − crossfade_band_fraction) × R₀`, no tier crossing is inside the
  shadow-casting set at all, so there is nothing for the missing dither to get wrong. *Struck: the earlier
  formulation, "cast shadows only from tiers 0–2, which the cascade arithmetic argues for anyway and which
  the 300–500 m horizon delivers for free."* **It does the opposite of what it claims.** Tiers 0–2 reach
  3.14 km, which *contains* both the tier-0/1 crossfade band (668–786 m) and the tier-1/2 band
  (1.33–1.57 km) — so with the shadow pass not honouring the dither, both rungs are fully opaque casters
  inside a band and the formulation guarantees the artefact twice rather than making it not arise. **Two
  named fallbacks** if the horizon ever has to exceed the bound: mark the fading-in rung a non-caster for
  the width of the band (trivial; the shadow itself then pops), or carry the dither into the shadow
  pipeline key (a small upstream patch, or a fork). D-R12 / D-RND-11 records both. This is a named gate in
  §8.4, not a defect to be discovered in the first flight test.
*Blocks.* The lighting slice; how the flight view reads.
*Cost of deferring.* Moderate. It is not a data format, but it is authored-content-adjacent: build
lighting gets art-directed around whatever horizon ships.

---

### 8.2 The one-way doors, consolidated

Every door this design opens, and the last moment it can be shut cheaply. "Shut by" is the phase
*before* which the decision must be recorded and the bits reserved — not the phase in which the feature
ships. **Rows 43–48 are added by the detail-level ladder; rows 14 and 42 are amended by it.**

| # | Door | Shut by | Cost of shutting it late |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The grid family | **Before P4** | Every planet in the galaxy; whether ships and planets share one grid |
| 2 | The warp curve on the cube-sphere | **Before P4** | Every block boundary on every planet; invalidates every stored edit |
| 3 | The planet radius **— now: the radius LADDER's step and the starter world's rung** | **Before P4** | The ladder step fixes grid resolution permanently; the per-body radius does not |
| 4 | Surface gravity, and therefore every sphere-of-influence distance **— now: derived from an authored per-body mass** | **Before P4** | Reshapes every star system if the derivation changes; the per-body value does not |
| 5 | The one-metre cell size (already answered) | Answered | A comparable title needed a new engine and a sequel |
| 6 | The width and layout of the saved block change | **Before P6 writes one edit; the chunk format depends on it at P4** | A migration over every saved planet, ship, station and blueprint |
| 7 | The block-identity model: one combined number, never independent fields | **Before P4 freezes the chunk format** | Same as above, plus it loses the property that an unapproved combination cannot exist |
| 8 | The numbering of substance, shape, function and block identifiers: dense, append-only, never reused | **Before P4** | Renumbering silently reinterprets every wall a player has built |
| 9 | The orientation field's width and the numbering of its twenty-four rotations | **Before P4** | Same silent reinterpretation, over every build ever made |
| 10 | The mirror flag, and the requirement that the shape catalogue be closed under mirroring | **Before P4** | Symmetry building silently punches holes in mirrored structures; the audit is over every shape, after players have built |
| 11 | Shape templates authored in cell coordinates rather than world coordinates | **Before P4** | It is the single choice that lets one catalogue be legal on a warped shell and a flat grid |
| 12 | One geometry per cell — no sub-cell subdivision | **Before P4** | A finer chisel layer must be strictly additive; making the base cell subdividable is the door a comparable title's sequel walked through |
| 13 | Explicit named shapes instead of a smooth density field | **Before P4** | Reversing means redoing the mesher, the vertex format, the collider path and the shading scheme together |
| 14 | The chunk address bit layout, including **FIVE** detail-tier bits at 60..56 *(amended twice — was three reserved, then four; five is what the ladder's top rung needs, and it is register row 1's second half)* | **Before P4** | A key-format migration over every saved world |
| 15 | Naming a world's database file after its immutable birth identity, not its current lineage | **Before P4** | Every interstellar trip renames a ship's block store; a crash mid-rename loses the interior |
| 16 | Where the noise comes from — **and that the sampler takes an octave count as a parameter** | **Before P4 generator code** | Regenerating every world underneath players' existing edits; a fixed-octave sampler makes the ladder a second code path |
| 17 | Whether mineral locations are computable from the shipped seed | **Before the client ships** | A schema migration plus a galaxy-wide regeneration |
| 18 | The texture tile period paired with the authored resolution | **Before the first material is authored** | Re-making every material by hand |
| 19 | Whether a second, higher-resolution hero texture array exists | **Before the material interface freezes (P4)** | Layer addressing propagates into the vertex word and every shader |
| 20 | The material identity carried in a vertex, and the single-index addressing all texture arrays share | **P4** | The mesher, the registry and every shader agree on it; changing it touches all three |
| 21 | The crumbling-edge amplitude, whether outward displacement is permitted, **and that it is metres rather than cells and is zero at tier ≥ 2** | **Before terrain art** | Art is authored against it; it also sets how much face merging survives on player builds |
| 22 | Which shapes are walkable | **Before the catalogue freezes (P4)** | Reversing breaks existing builds or trivialises them |
| 23 | The eight damage channels | **Before P6** | Cheap in code, but it re-derives and re-balances every material row |
| 24 | Whether the server light field carries colour | **Before P6b** | A rewrite of the mesher and the per-block state layout |
| 25 | Whether a per-block temperature exists at all | **Before P6b** | Fire and melting are both built on the answer |
| 26 | Whether unobserved worlds keep evolving | **Before P6 freezes the saved side tables** | A requirement on every mechanic, and it decides what is persisted |
| 27 | The decoration authority model, its hash input contract and its output bit assignment | **Before decoration slice 1 (P4)** | Changing either re-rolls every meadow, prop, clump and leaf cluster in the universe |
| 28 | The anchor-invariant global cell address | **P4** | It is the single thing that makes a world re-centring survivable without a whole-world visual regression |
| 29 | The four-triangle ceiling on a grass blade | **Before decoration art** | At twelve triangles the whole tier is three times over budget |
| 30 | The growth-log and decoration-override saved record shapes | **P6** | Persistence format; must survive a hard kill and a re-shard |
| 31 | The block-cover tag range and the block-configuration schema identifier | **P6 (reserved), P9 (used)** | A schema bump and a version-floor bump on every persisted block configuration in the world |
| 32 | The closed ten-command panel drawing set and its normalised coordinate space | **P9** | A wire contract |
| 33 | Whether a continuous control stream may ever be delayed by distance | **Before the signal wire shape freezes (P4 reservation, P9 use)** | Players build around zero-delay remote control; and once delay ships, station autopilot must be redesigned as uploaded programs |
| 34 | The width of the global channel identifier, with the loud collision check shipping in the first slice | **P9 slice 1** | A migration over every saved world once player-authored channel names are persisted at scale |
| 35 | Whether player scripting ever gets a real language | **Before scripting stage 3** | Removing or throttling a runtime players have written against is a community incident |
| 36 | Whether recipe rates may depend on their own accumulated state | **Before the first recipe exists** | A dormant world could never be caught up in closed form; the alternatives are re-simulating days of ticks or a world that does not advance |
| 37 | Whether articulated machines transfer as one entity or as independent sub-assemblies | **Before the block system lands (P6)** | A block system built on the latter cannot be retrofitted onto a single-entity handover without redoing both |
| 38 | The shape of the one new signal message family — one arm with a versioned envelope, not several | **P4 (written into the reserved block)** | If signals arrive as several message kinds the closed set passes thirty entries and the structural review that makes the sealed-world rule enforceable stops being reviewable |
| 39 | Whether voice is recorded for after-the-fact reporting | **Before voice ships** | Re-collecting consent from the entire player base |
| 40 | Whether radio is interceptable | **Before radio ships** | Opening a private channel later breaks everyone who relied on secrecy |
| 41 | Shipping recognisable bought art to players — **including any impostor atlas baked from it, which is a derived work under the same licence clauses** | **Before the first public build** | Establishes a visual identity that is expensive to change |
| 42 | The maximum sustainable flight speed *(amended — its derivation moved)* | **P4, once the MESHER and residency benchmarks run** | Ship performance gets tuned around it, which makes it a gameplay door as much as an engineering one |
| **43** | **The edit-pyramid entry layout, its key, and its storage-block granularity** | **Before the first world is saved** | Permanent delta data: a migration over every edited planet, ship, station and blueprint. Same class as door 6 |
| **44** | **The ladder's base — one rung per power of two, the tier a field on the chunk address and never a branch** | **P4** | Any other rung spacing breaks the octave-drop identity (tier L drops exactly L octaves), and a tier that is a code path rather than a number is an HR3 violation that spreads through the mesher, the material tables and the collider |
| **45** | **The requested-tier byte on the chunk / block-edit request lane AND the tier descriptor on its delta payload — one arm, both fields, landed together, because postcard is positional (D-39.6)** | **Before the P6 arm exists** | Free today — two bytes in a not-yet-written arm plus the four structural conformance tests. Afterwards it is a protocol-minor bump and a pyramid re-serialisation. Without it, coarse-first loading cannot ask for tier L without first pulling every tier-0 delta underneath it |
| **46** | **Variance-aware (Toksvig-in-the-mip-chain) roughness generation in the material bake** | **Before the first material is authored** | Re-baking every material. It cannot be fixed at runtime: two-channel BC5 normals make the averaged-normal length unrecoverable in the shader |
| **47** | **The write invariant — only tier 0 is writable, expressed in the store's type signature** | **P4.8, with the store skeleton** | Retrofitting it means auditing every writer instead of deleting an impossible call; and a pyramid written directly is a pyramid that can disagree with its deltas forever |
| **48** | **Bake-friendly authoring constraints on the prop archetype set** (clean silhouettes, no interpenetrating geometry) if decision 39 takes impostors | **Before prop authoring begins** | Re-authoring the archetype set for the bake |

---

### 8.3 The slice plan

**Thirty-seven slices across seven phase groups** *(was thirty-five; the ladder adds two — see P4.10 and
P4.11 — and folds the rest into existing slices).* **Sizes** are rough implementation effort, not
calendar: **S** ≲ 400 lines, **M** ≈ 400–1,200, **L** ≈ 1,200–3,000, **XL** > 3,000. Every slice inherits
the standing rule at the head of this section.

#### Phase 0 — plant slices, before any P4 feature code

These exist because retrofitting any one of them is a world migration or a simultaneous migration of
every producer. **Nothing in P4 may start before slices 0.1–0.4 land.**

**S0.0 — Measure the noise constant. ✅ DONE.** *Size: S.*
*Landed:* the timing binary and its published figures. **Measured on an Apple M4 Pro, one core: one noise
evaluation 12.19 ns; a complete 62³ surface chunk 0.885 ms**, using a height field plus a coarse-lattice
three-dimensional cave field sampled every fourth cell and interpolated.
*Consequence, stated plainly:* **the generation risk is closed.** At 0.885 ms per chunk, the 6,800-chunk
100 km view of the ladder is about 6 s on one core and 0.75 s on eight *before* counting the octave
saving, and coarse tiers cost strictly less. The alarming multi-second horizon this design was written
around does not exist.
*What moved as a result:* the maximum sustainable flight speed was to be derived from this constant
(one-way door 42). **It is not: generation is no longer the bottleneck.** The derivation moves to the
mesher-throughput and residency-under-motion gates in §8.4, which are now the unmeasured terms.
*Residual owed by this slice:* the per-tier curve — a tier-L chunk must be shown to cost strictly less
than a tier-0 chunk, which is the gate that proves octave-dropping is real rather than decorative.

**S0.1 — The geometry seam.** *Size: L.*
*Lands:* the one addressing type packed into a single machine word with its **five** detail-tier bits and
its zero-checked spare bits; the cell index type; the one chunk container with its palette and bit
packing; the geometry mapping with **all nine operations** — the six already specified plus the
fractional cell-point map, the cell-width bounds, and the chart-independent corner identity — **each
taking the tier as a parameter, so a tier-L cell is 2^L metres and nothing branches**; the seam table
derived and pinned; the frame-space reshape (the published chunk-address type replaced by the
sector-carrying address, plus the anchor-invariant global cell method); the determinism newtype that
makes the platform-varying maths functions unreachable on the generation path; and a frame-space shape
that *admits* more than one anchor while defaulting to one.
*Amended by Addendum 2 and corrected 2026-08-03 — the detail bits widen from three to **FIVE**, and here
is the arithmetic.* Three bits give tiers 0–7, which reaches 100 km at two pixels per cell; four give
0–15. **Neither expresses the ladder's true top rung**, which is data-derived — the rung at which one
chunk covers a whole cube face — and is **12** for the 162 km starter body, **18** for an Earth-sized one
and **20** for the largest addressable body. Five bits give 0–31 with eleven values to spare. *Struck: the
earlier "four bits … 3 + 3×18 = 57, and 57 + 4 = 61 of 64, three to spare".* That budget was computed
against Addendum 1's Earth-scale sizing rather than against the layout that actually exists. **§3.3.6's
layout is 3 (sector) + 5 (tier) + 20 + 20 + 10 = 58 of 64, SIX to spare**, all of them zero-checked on
decode. **Free today; a key-format migration over every saved world afterwards.**
*Done when:* the exhaustive mapping gate passes — neighbour lookup involutive on every seam cell, the
four-step lateral loop closing everywhere except the eight corner vertices where it closes in three,
every cell having exactly four lateral neighbours, address round-tripping for every cell, and the apron
gather watertight at all twenty-four boundary strips and all twenty-four corner-diagonal slots — at the
smallest configuration, which is a complete proof because the table does not depend on planet size; **and
the same enumeration passes at more than one tier** (decision 12).
*Run-anywhere fixture:* this slice *defines* the split gate (decision 12); the mapping itself carries
the exhaustive gate, everything above it carries equal-results.
*Must not regress:* the existing pose and coordinate tests; the demand-loop end-to-end runs.
*Planted here because:* every line written before this seam exists is written against an unknown
interface, and the retrofit is a rewrite of every producer plus its full-coverage tests.

**S0.2 — The block registry and the shape catalogue, declared.** *Size: L.*
*Lands:* the substance, shape, function and block-type registries in the core crate using the proven
generated-exhaustive-match idiom; the checked-in physical facts as constant data (no parser, no new
dependency); the derivation functions and the fourteen named scale constants; the append-only manifest
with a build failure if an already-issued row's meaning changes; the identity digest over
identity-bearing columns only, placed in the connection handshake and the store header; the **full
twenty-three-shape catalogue declared** with everything but the cube marked unplaceable; the frozen
twenty-four-rotation integer table and the mirror flag; the golden roster pin; **and the deterministic
coarse-shape table the edit pyramid's coarse cells are drawn through** (decision 37b) — indexed by the
entry's **octant mask and fill bucket**, 4,608 bytes, **folded into the block-registry hash so a mismatch
is a refused connection rather than a silently wrong distant silhouette**, with no tunable threshold
anywhere on the path — placed here because it must be identical on server and client and must be
exercised at every tier, which makes it core-crate Tier-A code rather than renderer code.
*Done when:* the six-part drift tripwire passes for all four registries, including the round-trip
assertion that a hand-edited row fails the build, and the identity digest is pinned.
*Must not regress:* the workspace's 100 % Tier-A coverage.
*Planted here because:* declaring the catalogue in full at P4 — even unplaceable — is what makes the
character-controller derivation well-defined from the first commit, and it is the cheapest commit in
the design and the only one that gets more expensive every week.

**S0.3 — The render seam widening.** *Size: M.*
*Lands, alone, while there is still exactly one producer: rotation on the primitive transform; indices;
the four build-bounded vertex streams; the pass class; the per-chunk header carrying the world-local
origin, the seed-derived salt, the occupancy slot, the biome and — **no longer "reserved" — a USED
`detail_tier` byte**, plus the two crossfade margin ranges per chunk entity.*
*Amended by Addendum 2.* The detail tier stops being a reservation and becomes the field the **material
feature ladder** is keyed on (decision 22, §8.6 item 9). It must be a **per-draw uniform**, not per-pixel
camera distance: a uniform weight makes the feature fade a branchless lerp, keeps it deterministic and
identical for every pixel of a chunk, and composes with the crossfade band instead of fighting it — a
per-pixel distance fade and a per-entity dither band disagree *inside* the band, which is where it shows.
The margin pair exists because the engine's own HLOD facility (`VisibilityRange`, documented as
"hierarchical level of detail" with dithered margins, driven per entity by camera distance and consumed
through one pipeline bit) is the crossfade mechanism — two rungs of the same column get complementary
ranges and the engine does the fade with no custom code.
*Done when:* the existing proxy scenes render byte-identically, and each of the three unused vertex arms
is constructed and exercised by a synthetic test — those synthetic constructions **are** the mesher's
future acceptance fixtures, written once and used twice.
*Must not regress:* every existing visual scenario, pixel-identically.
*Planted here because:* a rotating planet or a banking ship is already undrawable today; and after
terrain, edits, shaped blocks and hulls exist, widening is a simultaneous migration of four producers
plus their golden fixtures.

**S0.4 — The wire and transport plant slice.** *Size: L.*
*Lands:* two new client-facing routing classes — a reliable event class and a reliable-paced bulk class
— in one slice with their reliability mappings and their pinned discriminants, naming all their
consumers in the doc comments; the reliable client-to-server discrete-action carrier with the block-edit
arm and a reserved arm for the later fire trigger; two new saga step identifiers for the block-store
flush and the block-edit forward, taking the next unallocated numbers rather than repurposing an
existing one; four reserved step identifiers for durable signal configuration; the block-edit and signal
message-arm *shapes* written into the reserved block as prose; the fixed-point value type, the value
enum, the content-hashed channel and world keys with their loud collision check, and the copy-preserving
dedup key, all in the core crate; two appended world-kind tags for ships and constructions; a reserved
transferable kind for a voxel volume; and a reserved permission-token field.
*Added by Addendum 2 — two bytes and one prose paragraph, all free only until the arm exists.*
**(a) A `tier: u8` on the chunk / block-edit request shape AND a `tier` descriptor on its delta payload**,
landed together because postcard is positional, so a client can ask for tier L of a region without first
pulling every tier-0 delta beneath it, and the reply says which rung its entries are at. Today there is
**no** terrain-tier field anywhere: `intershard.rs:659`'s `coarsen_level` is a pose-precision hop counter
on `OccupantInterest`, and line 303 reserves the WHAT lane as a *concept*, not a field (see §8.0).
**(b) The edit-pyramid fetch shape written into the reserved block as prose**, alongside the block-edit
shape, so the coarse-before-fine ordering rule below has something to request.
*And one boundary this slice must not cross, settled 2026-08-03 because three sections had reserved three
different fields for one concept.* **Three ladders exist and none is derived from, or converted into,
another**, and every one of these fields carries a doc comment saying so: the chunk key's `tier` is the
chunk-local **content** ladder; `coarsen_level` is a **pose-precision hop counter**; and the only
observer-side tier is **`tier_floor`** on the client's area-of-interest report — a **client-declared,
server-clamped, non-authoritative hint** about client-local memory, in the same category as the
area-of-interest radius the client already declares. The server may use it for **egress selection only** —
which rung to send, and how often a telemetry channel is refreshed — and **no fence, arbitration outcome,
admission decision, scheduling deadline, persisted value or simulation state may read it, directly or
transitively.** *Struck accordingly:* `OccupantInterest::observer_tier`, `LedgerCell::min_demanded_tier`
and the protocol-minor bump raised for them. A shard's trajectory must be byte-identical for every value
of every observer's `tier_floor`, and §7's tier-invariance fixture now asserts exactly that.
*Done when:* the four structural conformance tests over the closed message taxonomy pass with the new
arms, and the stale prose arm counts in four files are re-synchronised with the code.
*Must not regress:* the whole transfer and chaos matrix.
*Planted here because:* three separate consumers need the reliable event class, four need the
discrete-action carrier, and a step-identifier collision aliases two different operations in a durable
journal — silently, and unrecoverably.

**S0.5 — The within-world area-of-interest reshape.** *Size: L.*
*Lands:* the per-cell spatial index and the per-subscriber addressing that replaces whole-world
broadcast.
*Done when:* the measured density fixture (128 sessions in one world) shows message counts proportional
to observers-with-that-chunk-resident rather than to observers times events.
*Must not regress:* the density fixture's correctness assertions.
*Planted here because:* **it is a precondition of block edits, not a follow-on.** The same index is what
chunk residency, delta manifests, edit fan-out, panel addressing and anchor partitioning all key off —
which is the argument for doing it once, first, with one consumer instead of five. Without it, panel
draw lists leak a private bridge's readouts to a stranger standing in the same station lobby. *One
addition:* chunk residency is now **per (chunk, tier)**, so the index's key gains the tier — free here,
a re-key later.

**S0.6 — Split the single sim shard file along capability lines.** *Size: L (mechanical).*
*Lands:* a mechanical decomposition of a 15,000-line file that already works around an engine arity
limit twice.
*Done when:* coverage is unchanged and the arity workarounds are gone.
*Planted here because:* the project's founding diagnosis blames three god-files for a third of its fix
commits, and this one file exceeds all three combined. Every later split is also a full-coverage test
reorganisation.

#### P4 — terrain generation and meshing

**P4.1 — The generator.** *Size: XL.*
*Lands:* seed-derived planet parameters through the existing integer generator with closed-form samplers
and no rejection loops; the height field sampled as three-dimensional noise on the unit sphere (so it is
continuous across all twelve edges and eight corners by construction); the strata table with its
saturating depth; biomes; **water as an ordinary material**; parametric-tube carvers; the ore overlay
split into a public half compiled into the client and a concealed server-only half; and the conservative
generator band with its stated invariant that it bounds *generated content only* and must be unioned
with the column's edit-presence bitmap wherever it is used as an emptiness answer.
*Added by Addendum 2 — the ladder's generator half, and it is a removal of work rather than an addition.*
**Octave dropping: tier L evaluates the same sampler with the top L octaves omitted.** No second sampler,
no precomputed pyramid, no second code path — the octave count is a parameter (door 16) and the tier is
already on the address. The three-dimensional cave field follows the same rule: caves below a coarse
cell's size correctly disappear. Two obligations ship with it:
- **The conservative band must be derived per tier**, because dropping octaves narrows the height range;
  a band computed at tier 0 and reused at tier 5 is wrong in the unsafe direction.
- **The envelope property, as a property test:** the tier-L height at a point must lie within the tier-0
  height's min and max over the coarse cell containing it. This is the proof obligation that makes skirts
  *provably* sufficient rather than merely observed to work — it **fixes the sign**, i.e. proves the crack
  can only open downward, so a downward apron always closes it. *Corrected:* it is **not** a bound the
  pyramid stores. The relief envelope it reads is §3.5.2's per-(tier, chunk column) min/max structure,
  **derived and never persisted** (decision 37a). And it does not stand alone: its companion is §3.5.6's
  `terrain_tier_agreement` bound, which **fixes the magnitude** of the disagreement. A skirt needs both,
  and either alone leaves a hole in the argument.
*Done when:* the same seed produces a byte-identical digest on three targets at two optimisation levels,
and the client crate and the sim crate produce equal digests for the same chunk list — **with the digest
set indexed by (seed, chunk key, tier) and the cross-build diff covering EVERY legal tier of the fixture
body**, not a sampled pair, because `h(dir, L)` is a different function per L and a tier that passes the
pin proves nothing about its neighbours. A coarse tier is terrain the player sees and is therefore under
the same determinism law.
*Must not regress:* the existing celestial determinism pin.
*Note:* the height-first ordering is worth 62×. With S0.0 measured at 0.885 ms per surface chunk, the
generator is no longer the risk it was written to hedge against.

**P4.2 — The integer mesher, cube lane only.** *Size: L.*
*Lands:* a new Tier-A crate **added to the coverage list in the same commit** (a crate omitted from that
list is silently exempt); occupancy masks, face-mask culling, greedy runs, and the integer chunk-geometry
output; the shared border-trimming operation, specified totally and exactly for every rectangle down to
one by one — **written first, because three separate cut rules consume it**; the two-material reduction
by lowest identifier, which is total, tie-free and chunk-independent.
*Added by Addendum 2 — **skirts land here**, in the mesher that owns them.* Each chunk emits a short
downward apron around its border, hiding the tier crack behind geometry never seen from above. About
twenty lines, **no case analysis, and — the property that decides it — no dependency on which tier the
neighbour is at**, which matters because that changes as the camera moves. *The depth is §5.9.4's derived
`skirt_drop`* — the relief across one cell of the **next coarser** rung, read from §3.5.2's derived,
never-persisted relief envelope, **plus the registry's maximum rim-warp amplitude**, times `skirt_safety`
(default 1.25), carried in the chunk header in that chunk's own cell units. The closed-form conservative
fallback when the envelope is not resident bounds it at about five cells at every rung. Aprons are emitted
unconditionally on the **four lateral borders only** — tier is assigned per chunk *column*, so vertical
neighbours are always at the same rung — which is a free 33 % saving and puts skirt geometry under 1 % of
a chunk's quads. *Alternative and why it loses:* vertex snapping / transvoxel is correct rather than concealed, but
it is a second lookup table (transvoxel's transition cells are 13 sample points and 512 cases) built for
smooth iso-surfaces, and adopting it means a second mesher and a second shape catalogue — an HR3
violation and precisely the fork Addendum 1 §A.2 rejected hex grids to avoid. Our surfaces are
axis-aligned quads at every tier, so two rungs meet in a vertical *step*, not an interpolated curve, and
a skirt closes it exactly. Held in reserve if skirts prove visible.
*Done when:* a fixed chunk fixture's quad list is pinned, and the throughput gate holds **as a per-tier
curve** (see §8.4 — this gate is promoted).
*Run-anywhere fixture:* one fixture meshing a chunk with a material seam, run on a spherical planet
profile and a flat ship profile, with equal results.
*Must not regress:* nothing yet — but the pinned quad list becomes the regression baseline for slices
P4.4 and P4.5.

**P4.3 — The encoder, the material and the texture arrays.** *Size: L.* **Preceded by a spike.**
*Lands:* the spike first — one extended material with one storage buffer and one per-instance tag,
drawing two chunks with different occupancy slots, on two graphics backends, to establish whether
extending a bindless base material can carry storage buffers at all; then the Tier-B encoder, the
extended material with three shared-index texture arrays plus a macro-variation array, the exact
integer-modulo world-space texture coordinates, and the anti-repetition layers with anti-tiling as a
per-material opt-in defaulting to off; **and the variance-aware roughness mip chain in the bake
specification** (decision 6, door 46) — a bake-tool change with no runtime cost that must exist before
any material is authored.
*Done when:* one planet chunk renders pixel-identically at the world origin and at a billion metres;
total video memory is asserted at start-up; and the forbidden shader-effect combinations are rejected by
a build-time assertion.
*Must not regress:* the mesher's pinned quad list.
*Note:* if the spike fails, the named fallback is a standalone material that reimplements the lit
fragment shader, at the cost of a re-merge every engine release. Ledgered.

**P4.4 — Material seam strips.** *Size: M.*
*Lands:* the seam predicate fired on the shared trimming operation, and the two-material ring shader
path with height-based selection, **dropped at tier ≥ 2 by the material feature ladder** — a blend across
a strip one cell wide is meaningless when the cell is 32 m.
*Done when:* a dirt-to-gravel boundary renders correctly at three quad sizes, and the tap count is
asserted from a shader-variant compile check **at tier 0 (≤ 32 taps, worst shipping configuration) and at
tier ≥ 4 (≈ 2 taps)**.
*Must not regress:* the merge ratio measured in P4.2 outside seam regions.

**P4.5 — The crumbling edge.** *Size: M.*
*Lands:* the rim-only displacement, computed on the processor in the Tier-A mesher and baked into the
vertex, keyed on the chart-independent corner identity from S0.1; the rim predicate as a 256-entry
constant table; the inward-bias derivation quantised to the project's existing fine lattice; the third
cut rule — any lattice point with a non-zero amplitude is a barrier in the greedy sweep — reusing the
same trimming operation; **and the tier rule from decision 11: the amplitude is in metres, is not scaled
by tier, and is exactly zero at tier ≥ 2**, which removes the merge barrier from every coarse chunk.
*Done when:* the golden-vector table of ten thousand corner configurations passes, including a mandatory
cube-face-seam continuity block and all eight cube corners; the exhaustive 256-configuration test asserts
no vertex moves outward through its own face plane and no displacement exceeds the amplitude; the
merge-ratio regression against P4.2 is inside its stated bound; **and a tier-2 chunk's quad list is
byte-identical with the crumble path enabled and disabled**, which is the assertion that the tier rule is
real.
*Must not regress:* the merge ratio on constructed materials, which must be exactly unchanged because
their amplitude is exactly zero.

**P4.6 — Transparency.** *Size: M.*
*Lands:* the second and third occupancy masks; the five face-emission rules; three pass classes with the
translucent class writing no depth and casting no shadow; water as a translucent material with an
animated scroll and depth-based absorption.
*Done when:* a water surface, a glass pane and a leaf card each render correctly against every other
class, and the mesher's stated cost increase for chunks containing transparency holds.
*Must not regress:* the opaque path's throughput.

**P4.7 — Decoration, tier one.** *Size: XL.*
*Lands:* the Tier-A evaluator (positional hash, the anchor-invariant key, the packed rule key, the flat
rule table, the micro-tier evaluator, the clump field as four hashes bilinearly interpolated in fixed
point, the shared crumbling-edge call so grass sits on the warped surface rather than floating above it);
then the render path — two compute passes, four phase registrations, one indirect draw over a variant
array with a loop fallback; the declared sim-to-decoration dependency edge with a module-boundary check
from the first slice; **plus the two ladder consequences: density falloff reaching zero (never a
visibility toggle), and the chunk's tier handing the evaluator its cutoff for free — no second distance
system**; and **hash-derived per-instance shape variation** (decision 25) as a few extra parameters in
the instance buffer, which costs bytes per instance rather than assets per archetype.
*Done when:* the golden-vector gate and the field-golden gate are in the pre-merge suite; the software-
adapter parity test diffs the two implementations; the frame-time gate holds on the reference tier; and
the paired visual scenario (place a soil block, place four hundred more, place a wood column and leaf
blocks, force a re-centring) asserts the pre- and post-re-centring frames are pixel-identical.
*Run-anywhere fixture:* the same place-soil-see-grass fixture on a spherical planet profile and a flat
ship-interior profile, and it must *mean the same thing on both* — which is why the "up" input is derived
from the gravity direction rather than being the raw grid face.
*Must not regress:* the frame budget; the mesher's output.

**P4.8 — The per-world block store skeleton.** *Size: L.*
*Lands:* the store named by an immutable birth identity that never changes when a ship flies between star
systems; the type-level single-writer proof (a writable handle obtainable only through a directory read
that returned this shard as owner, and a non-owner handle with no mutating method at all); the tuning
struct; the owed real-scale path-resolution inversion, which lands *with* the storage layer, not after
it; **and the tier-0-only write invariant expressed in the type signature — a write takes a tier-0
address, so `write(tier != 0)` cannot be written at all** (decision 37d, door 47).
*Done when:* a store refuses to open against a fence that is not strictly greater than the recorded one,
and double-open is detected by the fence rather than by a file lock (advisory locks over network
filesystems are unreliable and nothing may depend on them for correctness).
*Must not regress:* the durability suite.

**P4.9 — The shape bake and the derived controller constants.** *Size: M.*
*Lands:* the bake — templates authored in cell coordinates, the 48-transform orbit deduped by exact
integer vertex equality with winding reversed for improper transforms, the two coverage rasterisations
and the occlusion matrix, and the five closure assertions (total mirror closure, total group action,
exact volume equality with no tolerance, cell containment on the thirty-second lattice, and the connect
envelope); plus every character-controller length derived as an exact integer number of fine lattice
cells from the catalogue and the warp bounds.
*Done when:* all five assertions pass and the derived constants are checked in as pinned values.
*Must not regress:* the registry digest.

**P4.10 — Tier selection, the crossfade, and the material feature ladder. NEW.** *Size: M.*
*Lands:* the client-side half of the ladder, all of it reusing machinery that already exists.
- **Tier selection by screen-space error** — pick the tier whose cells subtend `px_per_cell_target`
  pixels — computed from the *same* angular-size rule the locked area-of-interest model already uses, one
  level down. **No second scheduler**, and nothing branches on realm kind or on tier.
- **The five tuning fields** of decision 38 in the render tuning struct — pixels-per-cell target and
  ceiling, the resident byte cap, the governor's hysteresis and the crossfade band fraction — with the
  resident-byte governor, its floor on tier 0's radius, and the assertion that it touches nothing
  gameplay-visible.
- **The crossfade**, through the engine's own `VisibilityRange` dithered margins: two rungs of the same
  column get complementary ranges and one pipeline bit does the fade. **With the fade-direction rule
  enforced in the code that assigns the margins — coarse fades in early, fine dies at its own range** —
  because the reverse costs +40 % peak residency instead of +10 %.
- **Coarse-before-fine as an ordering constraint on the request queue:** never request a fine tier for a
  region with no coarse tier resident. One resident-tier bitmask per column, near-zero CPU. This is what
  makes "the realm proxy is the coarsest rung" operationally true rather than merely conceptual — the
  proxy is the always-resident fallback that guarantees no hole during traversal.
- **The material feature ladder keyed on `ChunkHeader.detail_tier`** (decision 22, §8.6 item 9): fade the
  4 m detail tile out and the macro layer in, drop the normal map, drop parallax, drop the seam blend —
  all as branchless lerps on a per-draw uniform weight. **This is required, not optional:** at tier 5 the
  detail tile repeats 496× across one chunk, hardware mip selection returns its average colour, and
  without the ladder the coarse rungs look *worse* than no ladder at all.
*Done when:* the tier-count-under-load gate and the no-pop gate hold (§8.4), including the forward-walk
traverse at eye height, not only the flyover.
*Must not regress:* the frame budget; the demand-loop end-to-end runs, whose thresholds this shares.
*Why a slice of its own:* every bullet is a *client* concern with no server state, and bundling it into
P4.3 would put render policy inside the encoder.

**P4.11 — The long-range lighting answer. NEW.** *Size: M.*
*Lands:* decision 41's package. The **derived** shadow-map horizon across the engine's four cascades (a
compile-time ceiling, not a setting) — `shadow_max_distance = min(authored, (1 − crossfade_band_fraction)
× R₀)`, **668 m at the defaults**, asserted at start-up and **re-asserted whenever the residency governor
moves the pixel target** *(this replaces the earlier authored "300–500 m", which was a literal where the
relation is derivable, and it replaces "shadow casting restricted to tiers 0–2", which reached 3.14 km and
therefore contained two crossfade bands — it guaranteed the artefact rather than preventing it)*;
**terrain self-shadowing beyond the horizon computed by marching the octave-dropped height function along
the sun direction**, either per pixel or amortised into a per-chunk-column horizon-angle texture — no
shadow map, no cascade, no memory, and it cannot disagree with the drawn mesh because it is the same
function that produced it; the assertion that **a chunk's shadow-caster mesh is its visual mesh, one
object, both passes**, and that any separate shadow rung ever introduced is selected by the **light's**
screen-space error rather than the camera's; and **runtime geometric specular
anti-aliasing** (the projected-half-vector formulation, ~10 ALU and two derivative pairs per pixel, no
memory, no bake), which is needed *specifically* because §5.6 deliberately warps rim geometry — an entire
planet's worth of high-frequency geometric normals, now viewed at every scale from 1 m to 100 km.
*Done when:* the shadow double-cast gate passes at every tier boundary, and a mountain shadow falls
correctly across a valley at 20 km.
*Known and accepted limit, stated rather than hidden:* player-built geometry casts real shadows only
inside the cascade horizon.

#### P5 — physics

**P5.1 — The collider spike.** *Size: S but blocking.*
*Lands:* a reproduction of the cube-next-to-slope classification case and the chunk-seam case against
the pinned library version, plus the physics-state snapshot and restore determinism check that already
gates this phase.
*Done when:* the answer is recorded and decision 16 is closed. **This must run before the phase commits
to a collider architecture.**

**P5.2 — The four collision lanes.** *Size: L.*
*Lands:* cube cells on flat worlds through the library's voxel shape (subject to the spike); cube cells
on planets through greedy-box decomposition in cell space with boxes capped at eight cells per axis and
each box emitted as a convex hull over its eight mapped corners; shaped cells on flat worlds through the
baked collider templates with shared-shape deduplication; shaped cells on planets through per-cell warped
convex parts; collider residency bounded to a radius around dynamic bodies; and the rule that rigid-body
mass properties are computed from the block field with cell-nominal volumes, never from the collider
geometry.
*Added by Addendum 2 — one assertion, not a feature.* **Collision is tier 0 only, and the collider
builder refuses a chunk whose address carries a non-zero tier.** Not a policy in a document: a refusal in
the code. Tier 0 is resident wherever a player is, which is exactly where physics runs, so the constraint
costs nothing and closes the worst possible class of bug in a detail ladder — two players disagreeing
about where the ground is.
*Done when:* a character walked across a chunk boundary at twenty sampled offsets receives no vertical
impulse; the collider budget per dynamic-body cluster holds; collider construction from the block field
is bit-identical across binaries; and the tier-0 refusal is exercised.
*Must not regress:* the crash and chaos matrix.

**P5.3 — The character controller.** *Size: M.*
*Lands:* every threshold derived from the catalogue and the warp bounds rather than typed; the
separation assertion between walkable and non-walkable classes; the single trigonometric call evaluated
once per world at activation, quantised and carried in the world checkpoint so a re-home cannot change a
player's climb behaviour.
*Done when:* the derived constants match their pinned values and the separation assertion holds.

#### P6 — block edits and durable persistence

**P6.1 — The edit pipeline, and the edit pyramid.** *Size: XL.*
*Lands:* the reliable action carrier from S0.4 carrying a resolved target — cell, face, hit octant,
intended identity and orientation, and a nonce — with the server validating rather than re-aiming; the
two-stage protocol (an effect-free off-tick acceptance receipt plus the authoritative echo on the
applying tick); the full validation list (reach against the *server's* pose, line of sight, occupancy,
permission, the identity row exists which *is* the per-material admission check, orientation in the
derived legal set, the shape is placeable, pin permission, structural support, inventory, batch cap, rate
limit, nonce dedup); the append-only edit log with its sorted deterministic drain and the three-step
compaction checkpoint; the chunk record with its two encodings and the exact crossover; the forwarding
arm for edits arriving in overlap regions; the separate undo journal written in the same transaction; and
the fan-out rule that all edits committed in one tick for one chunk become one message per observer per
chunk per tick, addressed by chunk residency.
***And — this is the half Addendum 2 adds, and it is the whole of the ladder's real work — the sparse
edit pyramid.*** Maintained by the realm owner on commit of each edit batch, **inside the edit log's own
write transaction**: mark every touched cell's parent dirty, then for each rung in turn recompute each
dirty parent from its **eight children's summaries**, resolving a missing child through the **generator**
rather than through disk, **stopping at the first rung whose summary is unchanged** and *deleting* any
entry that comes to equal what the generator would produce. **≤ 1 entry write and ≤ 1 storage-block read
per rung per touched coarse cell; zero reads of the edit log; zero reads of any tier-0 delta.** *(The
earlier "at most eight small writes, **no disk read**" is struck: a parent is a function of its eight
children, so eight sibling summaries are read per rung — they lie in one storage block because the chunk
edge is even. See decision 37 for the cost arithmetic and §8.4 for the gate.)* Entry contents, keying,
storage granularity and the divergence policy are decision 37; the tier-0-only write invariant is already
enforced by the store's type signature from P4.8. Player-built structures have no generated baseline, so
their coarse tiers are *pure* pyramid, which is simpler rather than harder, and they degrade continuously
into the realm proxy. **The recompute-from-deltas audit command — `vdctl world verify-pyramid <realm>`,
which rebuilds every entry from generator plus deltas and asserts byte-equality — and its test-suite
assertion after every edit scenario land in this same slice, not later** — a derived structure that can
silently disagree with its source needs its audit built in from the start, or the first symptom is a
player noticing their tunnel is the wrong shape from a hilltop.
*Done when:* edits survive a hard kill and a re-shard; the log's byte output is deterministic; the
click-to-pixels budget holds; the fan-out is measured against the density baseline; **the
edit-survival-across-tiers gate passes (dig a tunnel, build a tower, fly away, confirm both are visible
at every tier boundary, fly back, confirm nothing popped)**; and **the pyramid recomputed from the deltas
is byte-identical to the incrementally maintained one**.
*Run-anywhere fixture:* one fixture placing and breaking a block on a planet profile and a ship profile,
**forcing a re-anchor mid-sequence** — this is the still-owed half of the existing re-anchor ledger item.
*Must not regress:* the transfer and chaos matrix; the density fixture.

**P6.2 — Damage.** *Size: L.*
*Lands:* the branchless integer gate-and-scale hit resolution; the four outcomes and their drop rules;
the sparse per-chunk side tables with their computed dense-promotion crossover and the loud per-world cap;
the eight-stage crack overlay as a change-driven, chunk-scoped delta; and the repair path as a separate
subtraction so the damage path stays monotone.
*Done when:* the resolution benchmark holds, the promotion crossover is measured rather than assumed,
and the replication cost at the density baseline is measured.
*Paired visual scenario:* a block damaged through all eight stages and healing back.

**P6.3 — The shaped lane.** *Size: L.*
*Lands:* the plate, ramp, corner and facet families made placeable; the resolve pass reading a
two-cell window and writing a resolved-variant buffer the mesher and the collider both consume unchanged;
the six face masks (full and partial per side) rather than one occupancy mask; **instancing, which is not
an optimisation but the mechanism that makes this lane bounded** — without it an ordinary decorative
facade produces 11 MB of geometry per chunk against a half-megabyte budget; sub-chunk mesh sections so a
single edit re-meshes an eighth of a chunk; and the sparse-iteration path for constructs occupying a small
fraction of a chunk.
*Done when:* the lane's hard per-chunk ceiling holds; a ten-thousand-block construct's full rebuild meets
its budget on the sparse path; and the adversarial checkerboard wall is inside the merge-barrier bound.
*Run-anywhere fixture:* a slope abutting a cube, on a planet profile and a ship profile.

**P6.4 — The build loop.** *Size: L.*
*Lands:* face-and-octant variant inference, look-direction auto-rotation against the derived legal set,
neighbour-derived connective sub-shapes with the pinned escape hatch living in the sparse state table
rather than in the orientation field, symmetry and mirror mode, batched line and plane placement (which is
both the latency mitigation and the re-mesh amortiser — four thousand edits, one re-mesh), and server-side
undo.
*Done when:* the shape sheet scenario — every distinct rendered placement laid out in a labelled grid, one
screenshot — passes on both a planet and a ship profile, turning a broken template, a reversed winding, a
wrong mirror twin or an off-lattice vertex into a pixel diff.

**P6.5 — Occupancy-based ambient occlusion.** *Size: M.*
*Lands:* the third occupancy mask uploaded as a sparse slab, ~~resident only within a short radius of the
camera~~ **resident at tiers 0 and 1 and absent above** — *amended: the old formulation was a private
radius carve-out invented under the no-detail-levels rule; with the ladder it becomes an ordinary rung of
the one ladder, which is both cheaper to reason about and removes a second distance system*; fragment-side
evaluation that is lane-agnostic by construction; and the exact rim sampling that uses the unwarped cell
index carried in the detail vertex, so a displaced position cannot index a neighbouring cell.
*Done when:* slab residency holds at the ground horizon, and the same scene is compared with the
screen-space stopgap and the occupancy path.

**P6.6 — Decoration, tier two, and edit reactivity.** *Size: L.*
*Lands:* declared read neighbourhoods and the reflected dirty set, always recomputed from scratch; the
